_notes.why: Neon's free plan caps the database at 512 MB, and at the cap every write in the app fails. These caps keep ingestion inside it; raise them after upgrading the plan. 0 or null switches a cap off.
_notes.max_live_per_company: Live crawled rows (active or stale) above the student levels one employer may hold; a board whose employer is at the cap inserts no more of them until rows close. 60 spreads the free plan's room across ~1,200 employers instead of letting a few giants (Walmart, HCA, Dollar General list thousands) fill it. Internship and new-grad postings are stored first and never held back by it (spec decision 1: the student feed must not shrink), and LinkedIn, Indeed and GitHub-list rows do not count.
_notes.skip_posted_older_than_days: A new posting the source dates older than this at first sight is not stored.
_notes.description_max_chars: Stored descriptions are cut here; hashes and extraction read the whole text. 12000 keeps every stored description whole (p99 10073, max 11817 on scraper-v2-dev, 2026-10-25).
_notes.max_new_rows_per_run: New rows one run (one cron-ats call, or one runner run) may insert.
_notes.stop_inserting_at_mb: pg_database_size above this stops inserts for the run (checked every 500 inserts); refresh and reconciliation go on. Neon's logical size runs about 36 MB above pg_database_size, so 400 keeps the branch near 436 MB, under the 450 MB gate and the 512 MB cap.
